Gowans Auctions, Moonah. Weekly Friday auction, Fri 2 Oct 2026

Gowans Friday auction

This is a general weekly sale, so most of the value is mass-market. All 1,352 lots were scanned with every photo viewed, and the 150 strongest candidates got a market pass with an Opus check. The best-supported picks are retro video games (lots 328, 746, 732, 489), LEGO sets (689, 672), boxed Funko Pop lots (806A, 890, 582A) and a Wild Turkey Rare Breed bourbon (329). They have plenty of sold comps but modest ceilings, from about $65 to $170 hammer. The more valuable-looking lots have no sold support, so they get no maximum bid and are listed under "Look at the inspection": gold rings and a signet ring (lots 7, 1, 5), an Omega Seamaster in a mixed watch lot (228), a 2009 Toyota Corolla (1C), a Honda outboard (1535), Tasmanian single malts (281 to 283) and a Mackie mixer, a Conn saxophone and other gear. Check weights, hallmarks and condition in person. Online absentee bids close at 9:30 AM Friday, and inspection opens at 8:30 AM.

Run details

Deadline
Online absentee bids close 9:30 AM Friday 2 Oct (Hobart). The live room auction starts at 10 AM, in lot order. After 9:30 AM, ring the office to leave an absentee bid. Winning bidders are emailed by 5 PM Friday. If two absentee bids are the same amount, the first one placed wins.
Inspection
Friday from 8:30 AM (Thursday 9 AM to 5:30 PM has passed). Gowans, 37 Main Road, Moonah, phone (03) 6278 1600.
Buyer's premium
19.8% including GST on the hammer price, on all lots except vehicles (contact the office). This is the auction's own notice, so the older 17.6% on the support page looks out of date. All-in = hammer x 1.198.
Mode
Lot data and photos came from Gowans' public API and image store. Read-only: no bids, logins or forms. There are no prices on this site, only a count of absentee bids.
Collection
Pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah. Inbound freight assumed $0 (local).
Page built
01/10/2026 23:13 AEST.
Blocked or login sources
eBay, Wine-Searcher and Australian Whisky Auctions are closed to this session (403 from the sites). Artrecord and AASD rate-limit and hide prices. No logins were tried.
Resume point
Workflow run wf_db784ad0-25e (script work/wf_gowans363.js in the repo). Batch files are in scans/ (g3_), one per batch.

Assumptions
  • All 1,352 lots in the auction were taken from Gowans' public API and image store and scanned with every photo viewed. None was unscanned. Lot numbers with a letter (such as 1C or 806A) are shown as the catalogue labels them.
  • This is a live room auction. The site shows no prices, only a count of absentee bids on each lot, so no current bid is used or shown. Scoring is blind to price.
  • Buyer's premium is 19.8% including GST on the hammer price for all lots except vehicles (contact the office), per the auction's own notice. All-in = hammer x 1.198.
  • 150 candidates with a blind score of 4 or more got a market pass. The other 90 candidates and the 1,112 lots the scan skipped appear in the table of every lot with a photo finding and a reason, but have no comps research.
  • Many sold prices come from marketplace and auction results data that does not say whether buyer's premium is included. Each card notes this where it matters. Maximum bids use only sold prices in the last 24 months.
  • Gold and silver weights, carat marks and maker claims in the titles are catalogue claims. The cards say where the photos support them and where they do not. Check weights and hallmarks at the inspection.
  • Pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah. Inbound freight is assumed to be $0 because you are local.
  • Sources closed to this session (eBay, Wine-Searcher, Australian Whisky Auctions) were not used.

Working and confidence

Why Medium: All four consoles identified from labels in the photos (MEGA DRIVE II, MASTER SYSTEM II POWER BASE, SUPER NINTENDO PAL VERSION). SOLD prices come from an opened aggregator page with dated individual sales, but eBay item pages could not be opened, sales are mostly overseas, many titles do not state condition, and the consoles are untested.

Dropped entries: Researcher supplied no entries. From the PriceCharting pages I left out: SNES Mini Classic sales (different product); boxed or bundled sales with controllers, leads or games (not comparable); a 'Broken Super Nintendo Console' at US$25.84 (known broken).

Working: Rate 1 USD = 1.438252 AUD. KEEP: lowest same-item SOLD per console: SNES 48.05 + Mega Drive II 13.49 x 2 + Master System II 13.35 = AUD 88.38; / 1.198 = 73.77, rounded down to $70. FLIP: resale as four separate untested console-only listings at medians: SNES 57.16, Mega Drive II 58.31 x 2 = 116.62, Master System II 57.45; total AUD 231.23. Less eBay AU fees about 13.4% = 30.99 and outbound postage about $15 x 4 = 60, net 140.24; / 2.396 = 58.53, rounded down to $55. Gowans premium 19.8%, pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0. Lot already has 10 bids.

Ask Gowans: Are any power supplies, AV or RF leads, controllers or games in the box? Have any of the four consoles been powered on? Is the second Mega Drive II complete (no cracks, cartridge flap intact)?

Working and confidence

Why Medium: Both cart labels read, and several SOLD entries checked on an opened page. But these are eBay sales gathered by PriceCharting (a retail audience, with only brief condition notes), the carts are untested, and the controllers may not be official.

Dropped entries: Dropped: researcher entry 2, the PriceCharting 'loose' average of US$24.60. It is a computed average, not a price paid, so it is not SOLD evidence. It is kept only as a cross-check. Researcher entries 1 and 3 were ranges bundling several sales. I split them into individual dated SOLD entries after checking each one on the page (all prices and dates matched). I left out the US$14.32 (with manual), US$11.26 (with players guide) and US$17.58 (German listing, unspecified) sales because they are not the same configuration. The researcher's assumed 1.50 rate is replaced with 1.4383, looked up live. Corrections: the second cart is Pilotwings 64, not a racing game, and the blue controller is third-party (it has an OFF/ON switch).

Working: Rate 1 USD = 1.4383 AUD. KEEP: lowest same-condition SOLD for each confirmed cart: Banjo US$13.48 = A$19.39 and Pilotwings US$4.58 = A$6.59, total A$25.98 / 1.198 = A$21.69, rounded down to $20. The grey controllers are left out of KEEP because I could not confirm they are official. FLIP: likely resale is about A$22 for the untested Banjo (middle of A$19.39, A$21.57 and A$25.03), about A$14 for Pilotwings, and A$36 for two grey controllers at a discounted A$18 each, total A$72. Less eBay AU fees of about 13% = A$62.64, less about A$8 for packing and postage shortfall over 3 to 4 parcels = A$54.64. Divided by 2.396 = A$22.80, rounded down to $20. The PC and PS2 games count as nil. Pickup from Moonah, inbound freight $0. The lot already had 9 bids when its page was saved, so it may well go past $20.

Rush 2 was dropped because the URL returned a strategy guide and the game is not in the lot. The researcher's rate of 1.54 was wrong; the live rate is 1.4383. The other carts are Nagano Winter Olympics '98, Wayne Gretzky's 3D Hockey, Beetle Adventure Racing and Pilotwings 64.

Working: Keep: this is a bundle, so I used the sum of each visible title's lower-quartile loose sale price. The absolute lowest sales are often lot breakups or damaged carts. US$76.16 x 1.4383 = AUD 109.5, / 1.198 = 91.4, rounded down to $90 hammer ($107.82 all-in). Banjo-Kazooie is left out until a cart is confirmed. Flip: likely resale is the sum of medians, AUD 157.1. Less eBay fees of about 13% (AUD 20.4) and about AUD 15 outbound postage, that leaves AUD 121.7. Divided by 2.396 = 50.8, rounded down to $50 hammer. If a genuine Banjo cart is confirmed: keep is about $120 hammer ((109.5 + 21.3) / 1.198) and flip about $60 ((183 x 0.87 - 15) / 2.396).

Working and confidence

Why Medium: I read the box numbers and convention stickers in the photo. Each figure has several dated sales on PriceCharting pages I opened. But they are US eBay sales seen through an aggregator (I could not open the eBay item pages), and box condition, which drives Funko value, has not been inspected.

Dropped entries: Dropped all 11 of the researcher's PriceCharting entries as filed. They were aggregate guide values filed as ASKING, not single prices paid. The researcher also misread PriceCharting's middle column as 'complete in box', but for Funko it means 'In Dmg Box' (figure in a damaged box). That is why the researcher's A$235 total undervalued a lot whose boxes look undamaged. I replaced them with dated single new-in-box sales from the same pages, filed as SOLD. Left out of the figures: chase, Target, FYE, Amazon and NYCC-only versions, invisible, red and chrome variants, multi-figure sets, damaged or 'not mint' boxes, and loose figures. Also corrected: the Snoopy sticker reads 2016 Summer Convention, not a generic exclusive sticker.

Working: Keep: lowest new-in-box sale for each figure in the last 24 months, in USD: Batman 4.99, Beast Man 9.00, Deadpool 26.00, Erlich 6.99, Predator 0.99, Interplanetary Batman 5.00, Kramer Golf 2.25, Kramer Good Cop 4.50, Okoye 3.50, Pajama Jack 2.50, Snoopy 11.00. Total US$76.72 x 1.4383 = A$110.34. Divided by 1.198 = A$92.10, rounded down to $90. Flip: likely resale is the median sales added up, US$230.40 x 1.4383 = A$331. Less eBay AU fees of about 13.4% plus A$0.30 per order x 11, about A$48. Buyers pay postage, packaging about A$2 x 11 = A$22. Net about A$261, divided by 2.396 = A$108.9, rounded down to $105. All-in cost at $90 hammer = A$107.82, at $105 = A$125.79. Pickup from Moonah, inbound freight $0.
